The report before you provides an update on the progress of the Fire Community Support Program. In July 2024 the South Student Fire Department assumed responsibility for the former Community Support Officer Program. The focus of the rebranded Fire Community Support Program was on minor social disorder offering supports to individuals while providing visible presence in the bids and to transit. The previous CSO Program did respond to transit related calls when necessary.

However, transit was not a primary focus of the previous program. Going recognition of the need for a more consistent physical and supportive presence on the transit system led to a strategic shift in priorities and an expanded mandate for the FCS program.

Through evaluation and listening to concerns from stakeholders and writers integration of transit support became a primary focus. This required a significant redesign of service delivery since the staff training close collaboration with transit leadership and frontline personnel.

The revised operational model implemented an early 2025 has enabled FCS teams to provide consistent non-enforcement based support across both transit downtown Riverstale and Broadway business improvement districts.

Balancing the priorities of transit and bid has been a challenge with current staffing levels. This have be had committed to allocating 50% of fire community supports time to transit and it has consistently reached only 46% a slight short fall that reflects the complexity of the call volume and as well as transit related incidents that the fire community support has been providing services to.
The fire community support program continues to demonstrate its value resolving the vast majority of transit related incidents without police involvement.
It is evident that sustaining and expanding the fire community support reach will require consistent and careful review of available resources.
While transition has presented challenges the results speak to the value of the service delivery redesign the SFD remains committed to working collaboratively with transit beds and our stakeholders.
Future reporting is slated for September of 2025 after a full review of our community support program from the date of transition in July of 2024.
